newsitem.title: USA: Loctite hits all-time high on Henkel offer.
newsitem.headline: Loctite hits all-time high on Henkel offer.

text.p: Loctite Corp shares soared more than 26 percent to 58 in Monday morning New York Stock Exchange trading after Henkel KGaA of Germany said it intends to acquire for $56 per share the 65 percent of Loctite it does not already own.
Earlier in the session Loctite's share price reached an all-time high 59, up 13 from Friday's NYSE close, eclipsing its previous peak of 53-3/4, reached in early March.
Loctite said it would review the Henkel proposal. It declined to comment further.
Based on Loctite's 32.02 million shares outstanding, the Henkel offer is worth about $1.165 billion.
In a statement, Loctite said it, its directors and management "and their various advisers will obviously review this proposal to determine the proper response."
"We will also bear keenly in mind the effect any of this may have on our worldwide employees, whose everyday contribution and commitment make Loctite the quality company it is," it said.
Loctite said Henkel has been a major shareholder since 1985 and occupies three of the 12 seats on Loctite's board.
Earlier, Henkel said it would seek a friendly transaction but said if progress is not made, it might launch a public takover.

Loctite, based in Hartford, Conn., manufactures chemical adhesives, sealants and coatings, primarily for automotive applications. Last week it reported third quarter earnings of $0.72 per share on revenues of $201.8 million, versus $0.65 per share on revenues of $195.8 million a year earlier.
